name: George Francis Adams (#1)

Served in the Confederate army during the Civil War under Generals Price, Van Dorn, and McGruder

Per the 1898 biography: farmed in Jefferson County, VA, then moved to Chariton County, MO onto War of 1812 grant prairie land; pre-empted 160 acres at 12.5 cents an acre, built up to a full section devoted to stock, served as justice of the peace, came to Colorado in 1886 and lived retired until his death at 81.
His grave lies between the graves of two of his daughters, Virginia and Harriet; his son James is buried in the next row at his feet.

His obituary, signed "A Friend", says he was born in Jefferson County, Virginia; his parents went west in 1833; he went back to Virginia in 1834 and returned to Missouri the same year; fought in the Black Hawk War (printed 1835), enlisted under General Price and Colonel Watson to drive the Mormons from Missouri (printed 1836), and later against the Mexicans to capture Santa Fe; served in the Confederate army under Generals Price, Van Dorn and Magruder; was a large landowner who lived 42 years in Chariton County, Missouri, came to Colorado in 1878 and lived there until his death; his wife died in 1863; he raised his children himself and left four sons and four daughters. [Obituary of George Francis Adams, Castle Rock Journal (Castle Rock, Douglas County, Colorado), 12 Aug 1896, p. 4]
